diagnostic_evidence.quote: While our architecture inherently ensures symplecticity, exact Hamiltonian conservation is not enforced, as the proposed architecture only guarantees an approximate Hamiltonian is enforced.
To explicitly maintain Hamiltonian invariance, particularly crucial for complex nonlinear systems, we introduce an additional Hamiltonian conservation constraint:

issues.failure_explanation: The text claims that preserving the symplectic structure "ensur[es] energy conservation and numerical stability". Symplecticity preserves only the two-form: a symplectic map (the latent HénonNet flow, the encoder/decoder) need not conserve H and need not be stable. The paper itself later states that "exact Hamiltonian conservation is not enforced" and that H enters only through the soft penalty L_ham, so the advertised guarantee is both mathematically false and internally contradicted.

failure_location.quote: In summary, our architecture maintains the symplectic structure of the original system, ensuring energy conservation and numerical stability through nonlinear transformations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the guarantee: the architecture preserves the symplectic form exactly while the Hamiltonian is only approximately preserved through the penalty L_ham (as Section 4 already states), and delete "energy conservation and numerical stability" as structural consequences.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised structural guarantee of energy conservation (and numerical stability as a consequence of the architecture) is unsupported; Hamiltonian behavior can only be claimed approximately/empirically through L_ham. No labelled formal result relies on this claim.
issues.title: Symplectic architecture falsely claimed to ensure energy conservation
issues.why_classification: The repair is a limited weakening of an advertised guarantee: no new argument or construction is needed and the symplecticity results and empirical claims survive, but a promised guarantee type (energy conservation) must be withdrawn, so it exceeds a local fix that preserves all guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: For the displayed map the Jacobian is [[0,I],[I,H_V]], so (DH)^T J_{2n} (DH) = -J_{2n}: the mapping reverses the symplectic form instead of preserving it. Only its even powers are symplectic, which is exactly why the layer is defined as the fourth power H(V,eta)^4. The stated reason that the elementary mapping preserves symplectic structure is therefore false.

failure_location.quote: The fundamental building block is the H\'enon mapping, which enables intricate nonlinear transformations while preserving symplectic structure:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the statement: H(V,eta) satisfies (DH)^T J (DH) = -J (anti-symplectic) while the layer H(V,eta)^4 is symplectic; symplecticity of HénonNets then follows from composition of layers.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the building block itself preserves the symplectic form is wrong, and any construction using an odd power of the Hénon mapping would destroy the structure. Because layers are fourth powers, the Hénon layer, the HénonNet and the embeddings built from them remain symplectic, so no labelled result collapses.
issues.title: Hénon mapping is anti-symplectic, not symplectic
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction of the claim preserves every guarantee the paper actually needs (layers and networks are symplectic as stated elsewhere); no argument or construction is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: iota^+ is 2k x 2n, so (iota^+)^T J_{2n} iota^+ is 2n x 2n and cannot equal J_{2k} (2k x 2k); concretely, with iota^+ = iota^T one gets iota J_{2n} iota^T = blockdiag(E E^T, -E E^T) != J_{2n}. The valid relations are iota^T J_{2n} iota = J_{2k} and iota^+ J_{2n} (iota^+)^T = J_{2k}. Also iota^+ iota = I_{2k} has infinitely many solutions because iota is rectangular, so it does not "uniquely define" iota^+ (eq:symplectic-inverse does).

failure_location.quote: The symplectic pseudo-inverse $\iota^+$ is uniquely defined by the condition $\iota^+ \iota = I_{2k}$ and satisfies $(\iota^+)^T J_{2n} \iota^+ = J_{2k}$, ensuring that the inverse mapping preserves symplectic structure on the embedded submanifold.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false identity by iota^+ J_{2n} (iota^+)^T = J_{2k} and define iota^+ by eq:symplectic-inverse rather than by uniqueness of a left inverse.
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification for symplecticity of the inverse composite embedding on the embedded submanifold is invalid and the pseudo-inverse is mischaracterized; the conclusion itself still follows since sigma is a symplectic embedding with left inverse sigma^{-1}.
issues.title: False and dimensionally inconsistent symplectic pseudo-inverse identity
issues.why_classification: A short local correction of a stated identity preserves every claim; the surrounding conclusion about sigma^{-1} remains true without new work.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The universal approximation capability of H\'enonNets implies that any symplectic diffeomorphism, including the nonlinear embedding defined above, can be approximated arbitrarily closely by composing a fixed linear embedding with H\'enonNet transformations.
Let $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{2k}\to\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ be an arbitrary symplectic embedding defined on a compact domain $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^{2k}$.

Thus, while general nonlinear symplectic embeddings may utilize learned linear embeddings \(P\), the practical equivalence due to universal approximation allows us to adopt a simpler, fixed embedding strategy.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts that every symplectic embedding Phi of a compact domain in R^{2k} is uniformly approximable on that domain by maps H o G o iota, i.e. by the restriction of one global symplectomorphism of R^{2n} composed with the fixed inclusion. No proof is given. The only stated reason invokes a universal approximation theorem for symplectic diffeomorphisms of the ambient space R^{2n}; that theorem concerns diffeomorphisms of R^{2n}, not embeddings R^{2k} -> R^{2n}, and does not imply that a given Phi is approximable by phi o iota. Closing the gap requires a nontrivial extension/approximation result for symplectic embeddings of compact domains (extend Phi to a symplectomorphism of R^{2n}, or approximate it by such restrictions), which is neither stated nor cited.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the missing argument: prove or cite that every symplectic embedding of the compact domain Omega (with the needed regularity hypotheses) extends to, or is uniformly approximable by, a global symplectomorphism of R^{2n}, then apply the HénonNet approximation theorem on a compact neighborhood of iota(Omega); if such a statement needs hypotheses on Phi or Omega, state them and weaken the theorem accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: thm:universal-approx is unsupported, and so are the derived claims that fixing the canonical inclusion loses no approximation accuracy and that the HénonNet/G-reflector constructions give complete parametrizations of the nonlinear symplectic embedding manifolds in Section 5.
issues.title: Universal approximation theorem for symplectic embeddings is unproved and mis-justified
issues.why_classification: A contained nontrivial lemma (extension of symplectic embeddings) plus a standard approximation-transfer step would establish the theorem, and at worst a limited narrowing of the class of Phi/Omega leaves a recognizably comparable universal-approximation result; no new global proof architecture or loss of the ROM method is required.

issues.failure_explanation: For the stated initial-boundary value problem with u(0,t)=u(1,t)=0, the formula u(x,t)=u^0(x-omega t) is only the pre-reflection part of the solution. Once the right-moving bump reaches x=1 (which happens inside the reported window 0<=t<=24 for the stated omega, a_0 and x_0 ranges), u(1,t)=u^0(1-omega t) != 0, and odd image terms such as -u^0(2-x-omega t) are required. Hence the displayed formula does not solve the stated problem outside a short initial interval.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula by the odd-reflection (d'Alembert) solution of the Dirichlet problem, or restrict the claim to the time interval before the wave reaches x=1.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed exact solution of Example 1 is false in most of the simulated time window, so any validation or comparison based on it is unreliable.
issues.title: Claimed exact solution of the linear wave problem ignores boundary reflections
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the statement (add the image terms or restrict the validity interval) preserves all method claims and results; no new argument, construction or reoptimization is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: With z=(q,p) the displayed quadratic Hamiltonian has grad_q H = -omega^2 Delta x D_xx q and grad_p H = Delta x p, i.e. grad_z H = Delta x(-omega^2 D_xx q, p); but the displayed L gives Lz = (q, omega^2 D_xx p). The asserted identity grad_z H = Lz is false (blocks on the wrong diagonal, wrong sign, missing Delta x factor), and J L z would generate q_t = omega^2 D_xx p, p_t = -q rather than the central-difference discretization q_t = p, p_t = omega^2 q_xx claimed in the same paragraph; with the displayed H itself, dot z = J grad H is a time-rescaled system (q_t = Delta x p). Example 2 repeats the same matrix and additionally writes omega^2 where the coefficient is kappa(omega); since omega there is a four-vector, omega^2 is not even a defined scalar.

failure_location.quote: \frac{d}{d t} \mathbf{z}=\bbJ_{2 N} \nabla_{\bf z} H({\bf z})=\bbJ_{2 N} L \, \mathbf{z}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the semi-discrete system consistently, e.g. take H = (1/2)||p||^2 - (omega^2/2) q^T D_xx q so that grad H = (-omega^2 D_xx q, p) and q_t = p, p_t = omega^2 D_xx q, set L equal to that matrix (fixing the Delta x normalization), and use kappa(omega) in place of omega^2 in Example 2.
issues.overall_effect: The stated semi-discrete systems and the claimed Hamiltonian structure of Examples 1 and 2 are unreliable as written: both the operator generating the reference dynamics and the identity used to claim Hamiltonian structure are wrong.
issues.title: Discrete Hamiltonian gradient identity is false in Examples 1 and 2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of the displayed operator and normalization; the discretization, the method and all reported claims and guarantees survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Differentiating the displayed H_cont with the convention dot z = J grad H gives q_t = -2 p_xx + 2 epsilon (q^2+p^2) p and p_t = 2 q_xx - 2 epsilon (q^2+p^2) q. No overall constant reconciles this with eq:schro-can: the relative sign between the dispersive term and the epsilon-term is opposite. The Hamiltonian generating eq:schro-can is the NLS energy with opposite-sign terms, e.g. int[-(q_x^2+p_x^2)/2 + epsilon (q^2+p^2)^2/4] dx. As displayed, H_cont is not conserved along solutions of eq:schro-can.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the relative sign (and matching overall factor) between the gradient term and the epsilon-term of H_cont so that it generates eq:schro-can.
issues.overall_effect: The Hamiltonian claimed for Example 3 is neither the conserved quantity nor the generating function of the stated dynamics, so the Hamiltonian-conservation evidence of that example is mis-specified at the continuous level.
issues.title: Continuous Hamiltonian of Example 3 does not generate the stated NLS system
issues.why_classification: A one-sign local correction restores consistency with the stated canonical equations; the example, the method and all conclusions are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{d}{d t} \mathbf{z}=\bbJ_{2 N} \nabla_{\bf z} H({\bf z})=\bbJ_{2 N} L\mathbf{z} + \bbJ_{2 N}\mathbf{g}(\bf z),

issues.failure_explanation: The first two terms equal q_i^2 (q_{i-1}-q_i)^2/Delta x^2 and p_i^2 (p_{i-1}-p_i)^2/Delta x^2, not the discrete gradient energy (q_{i-1}-q_i)^2/Delta x^2, so their gradients do not produce the discrete Laplacian D_xx occurring in L. The nonlinear term epsilon(p_i^2+q_i^2)/4 has degree two, whereas only (epsilon/4)(p_i^2+q_i^2)^2 has gradient with entries (q_i^2+p_i^2)q_i and (q_i^2+p_i^2)p_i as in the displayed g. Hence grad_z H = Lz + g fails and the displayed H is not conserved by the stated semi-discrete flow; the normalization/sign is also inconsistent with L = diag(D_xx, D_xx), for which the quadratic part must be (1/2) z^T L z.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite eq:schro-ham-discre as the discrete energy consistent with dot z = J(Lz + g), e.g. H = (1/2) z^T L z + (epsilon/4) sum_i (p_i^2+q_i^2)^2 (equivalently -sum_i[(q_i-q_{i-1})^2+(p_i-p_{i-1})^2]/(2 Delta x^2) + (epsilon/4) sum_i (p_i^2+q_i^2)^2), fixing the Delta x normalization consistently with L and g.
issues.overall_effect: The identity dot z = J grad_z H = J L z + J g claimed in Example 3 is false as written, and the "discrete Hamiltonian" whose conservation is displayed in that example is not defined consistently with the dynamics.
issues.title: Discrete Hamiltonian of Example 3 is not a Hamiltonian of the stated semi-discrete system
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local rewrite of one energy formula by routine algebra; the example, the claimed Hamiltonian structure and all conclusions and guarantees survive.
